headline: ‘Bottom of Your Boots’ Still Number One; Moroney Enters Top 10, Langley Debuts ‘Broken’
body: [[Ella Langley]] holds the top spot on the Hot 20 for a third week with ‘Bottom of Your Boots,’ her seventh #1 single. She also earns the week’s Hot Shot Debut, as ‘Broken’ enters at #17, giving her two songs on the chart. Underneath Langley, [[Kenny Chesney]] holds the #2 position for a third straight week with ‘Silver Sands Marina,’ and [[Ingrid Andress]] stays at #3 with ‘Tattoos.’ Behind them, three singles reach new peaks. [[Emily Ann Roberts]] rises 5-4 with ‘Laundry,’ [[Mackenzie Carpenter]] climbs 6-5 with ‘Kinda Want Your Man,’ and [[The Castellows]] move 7-6 with ‘Love Is A Game.’ In fact, Carpenter has now taken all four of her Hot 20 entries into the Top 5. [[Wyatt Flores]] climbs 8-7 with ‘Hate Myself,’ another new high. [[Kip Moore]]’s ‘Faith in the Wind’ slips 4-8, one week after reaching its peak, while [[Carly Pearce]] rises 10-9 with ‘She Don’t.’ Rounding out the Top 10 is [[Megan Moroney]], who moves 11-10 with ‘Medicine.’ Remarkably, all nine of her Hot 20 entries have now reached the Top 10. Just outside, [[Riley Green]] rises 12-11 with ‘Imagine That,’ and [[Ashley Cooke]] earns the Greatest Gainer trophy, jumping 17-12 with ‘High School Sweetheart.’ [[Flatland Cavalry]] also gain five spots, rising 18-13 with ‘Never Coming Back.’ Kacey Musgraves’ ‘Mexico Honey’ slips 13-14, and her four-week leader ‘Loneliest Girl’ falls 9-15. [[Alana Springfield]] holds at #16 with ‘Love Me Anyway,’ while [[Maddie Font]] (‘Drive Me Around’) and [[Carter Faith]] (‘If I Had Never Lost My Mind’) each move down one rung, 19-18 and 20-19. Closing out the chart is [[Miranda Lambert]], whose ‘Two Things Can Be True’ debuts at #20. It is her 34th Hot 20 entry, one shy of Carrie Underwood’s record. Making room, Mackenzie Carpenter’s ‘All In Already’ and Flatland Cavalry and Kaitlyn Butts’ ‘A Life Where We Work Out’ fall off the chart.

On the Pop 10, [[Cassandra Coleman]] spends a third week at #1 with ‘End of Your Love.’ [[Roxy Dekker]] holds at #2 with ‘Ver Van M’n Bed,’ while [[Aitana]] climbs 4-3 with ‘6 of Febrero,’ a new peak and her fourth Top 5 hit, though she is still looking for her first #1. [[Karol G]]’s 1-week leader ‘Alguien Que Te Amaba’ slips 3-4. The Greatest Gainer is [[Peach PRC]], whose ‘Eucalyptus’ jumps 8-5 to a new high, and [[Adela]] also gains three spots, rising 9-6 with ‘Nicole Kidman.’ [[Taylor Swift]]’s ‘Patient Zero’ falls 5-7 and [[Ellie Goulding]]’s ‘Black Prada Dress’ slips 6-8. [[Ashe]] moves 10-9 with ‘Stop the Wedding’ in its second week. The week’s only debut comes from [[Olivia Rodrigo]] and [[Chappell Roan]], whose ‘Expectations’ enters at #10. It is Rodrigo’s eighth Pop 10 entry and Roan’s tenth. To make room, girlsweetvoiced’s three-week leader ‘Cranberry’ falls off the chart from #7.

headline: ‘Bottom of Your Boots’ Still Number One; Emily Ann Roberts Enters Top 5
body: [[Ella Langley]] remains atop the Hot 20 for a second week with ‘Bottom of Your Boots.’ The single is Langley’s seventh #1, and remarkably, every one of her 11 entries on the chart has reached the Top 5. Underneath Langley is [[Kenny Chesney]], who holds the #2 position for a second week with ‘Silver Sands Marina.’ It is his highest charting single since 2019’s ‘Tip of My Tongue.’ The big mover this week is Kacey Musgraves’ four-week leader ‘Loneliest Girl,’ which falls 3-9. Because of this, the next six singles each climb one rung. [[Ingrid Andress]] rises 4-3 with ‘Tattoos,’ a new peak in its 15th week, while [[Kip Moore]] moves 5-4 with ‘Faith in the Wind,’ which reaches a new high in its 22nd week on the chart. New to the Top 5 is [[Emily Ann Roberts]], who rises 6-5 with ‘Laundry,’ her first career Top 5. [[Mackenzie Carpenter]] climbs 7-6 with ‘Kinda Want Your Man,’ [[The Castellows]] move 8-7 with ‘Love Is A Game’ and [[Wyatt Flores]] rises 9-8 with ‘Hate Myself,’ his first Top 10. [[Carly Pearce]] holds at #10 with ‘She Don’t.’ Just outside the Top 10, [[Riley Green]] earns the week’s Greatest Gainer trophy, jumping 14-12 with ‘Imagine That,’ while [[Kacey Musgraves]] rises 15-13 with ‘Mexico Honey,’ giving her two songs in the Top 13. There are no debuts this week, with #16 through #20 holding in place.

On the Pop 10, [[Cassandra Coleman]] holds #1 for a second week with ‘End of Your Love,’ her fifth #1 single. In fact, the entire Top 7 stays put this week, the first time that has happened in at least a year. [[Roxy Dekker]] remains at #2 with her 1-week leader ‘Ver Van M’n Bed,’ ahead of [[Karol G]]’s 1-week leader ‘Alguien Que Te Amaba’ at #3 and [[Aitana]]’s ‘6 of Febrero’ at #4, meaning three of the Top 4 are sung in a language other than English. [[Taylor Swift]] holds #5 with ‘Patient Zero.’ Interestingly, Swift has now placed eight songs on the Pop 10 but is still seeking her first #1. [[Ellie Goulding]] stays at #6 with ‘Black Prada Dress’ and [[girlsweetvoiced]] holds #7 with the three-week leader ‘Cranberry.’ Below them, [[Peach PRC]] rises 9-8 with ‘Eucalyptus’ and [[Adela]] climbs 10-9 with ‘Nicole Kidman,’ both new peaks. [[Ashe]] is the week’s only debut, entering at #10 with ‘Stop the Wedding,’ her first appearance since 2021’s #1 ‘Till Forever Falls Apart.’ Coleman’s ‘Midnight Blue’ falls off the chart from #8 to make room.
